\caption{Every optimization, put back one at a time, on the whole genome (D6-ONT24K, REF-HS1). The leftmost bar is the C++ itself; \emph{pre-optimization} is this port with every ablatable change switched off (\texttt{SHMAP\_ABLATE}), and each rung to the right switches exactly one more back on, so adjacent rungs differ by one change and nothing else. End to end the C++ is 2.64$\times$ the shipped mapper here, of which 2.15$\times$ is the port itself and 1.23$\times$ the ladder; the product returns the first. The two series are the two thread counts: their gap is row~4, row~8 is not ablatable, and the C++ has no \texttt{-@N} counterpart. Left: wall clock, median of 5 round-robin runs of the whole ladder, whiskers at min--max. Right: peak resident set, log scale; the accumulator the first change removes is sized by the reference and allocated \emph{per worker}, which is why the \texttt{-@8} baseline stands above even the C++. Every rung's mapping is byte-identical; the run fails otherwise. Numbers, per-stage timers and the decomposition in \texttt{figure\_ablation.tsv} and \texttt{reconcile.tsv}.}
